composition.title: Crosswind Modal
composition.key: D lydian, with A mixolydian and B aeolian colours
form: A, bars 1-8: D lydian (Dmaj9#11 alternating with E/D) with Bm11 and Cmaj9#11; kick, electric piano, bass and ride accents grouped 5+5+6 so the bar feels like quintuple phrases inside 4/4 while the snare keeps the backbeat; the scooping lead sings long tones; ensemble hits on 1, a2, 2+, 3, 3a, 4e with a tom answer in bar 8.

B, bars 9-16: A mixolydian with chromatic-mediant shifts (A9 | Cmaj9 | A9 | Fmaj9#11 | Bbmaj9 | Gm9 | Ebmaj9#11); everything regroups as 3+3+2 hemiola, the lead plays dotted-eighth arches, the supersaw pad moves in half notes against it; A7sus4 ensemble hits and a tom run.
A', bars 17-24: the lydian A changes again with the lead varied and soaring to F#6, G#6 and A6 in bars 20-23; the same ensemble-hit bar 24.

C, bars 25-32: B aeolian/D major chain Bm9 | Gmaj9#11 | Em11 | F#7alt twice (Cmaj9#11, A13sus4 on the second pass) grouped 3+3+4+3+3, with lead, bass and piano all landing on the group starts, and a full tom roll into bar 1.
composition.motif: An A-D pickup to a long F#, then the lydian G# leaning up to A (the raised fourth resolving to the fifth); every lead note scoops up one and a half semitones like a portamento synth; B recasts it as 3+3+2 hemiola arches, C as 3+3+4+3+3 phrases.
composition.intent: Lyrical late-70s jazz fusion rather than overdriven: straight sixteenths with odd accent groupings inside 4/4 (5+5+6 in A, 3+3+2 hemiola in B, 3+3+4+3+3 in C) spelled by the kick, the ride accents, the electric-piano comping and the bass, while a light backbeat snare with ghosts keeps the 4/4 underneath; ensemble hits with tom answers at phrase ends; a soft sawtooth lead with a negative pitch envelope (portamento-like scoops), vibrato and delay; FM electric piano rootless lydian voicings (maj9#11, E/D slash, m11, 7alt, 13sus4); a slow phased supersaw pad counterline in half notes; a round fretless-like triangle bass with a small scoop. Lydian and mixolydian colour with chromatic-mediant moves. Distinct from 61 (120 BPM E dorian overdriven head and slash-chord planing): slower, lyrical, D lydian, no distortion, different groupings and a pad counterline.
